---
description: self_read as the model is told it - what the tool does, and what each of its arguments is.
doing: reading your own record
arguments:
  part: "Which part of your record: perceptions (what you perceived and have not yet taken in), imported (your old mind files not yet filed), memories, relationships, knowledge, history or game-side. Leave it out for every part, with how many entries it holds and how large it is."
  id: "One entry, by its id. With to, the first of a range."
  to: "The last id of a range that starts at id, both read. Alone, everything up to it."
  day: "perceptions, memories, history: only those of this day, written as your outline writes it."
  scene: "perceptions: only those of this scene, by its id, as your outline names it."
  name: "imported: the file's name (core.md; minds for the notes the older minds pack kept). relationships: the person. memories, knowledge: only what is about this person or thing, or what they told you."
  subject: "Only entries that hold all of these words."
  tier: "memories: only those at the top of your mind (top), from lately (short) or from longer ago (long)."
  skip: "Skip this many entries first, to read on in a long answer."
  how: "gist: each entry by what your record holds that stands for it (a memory's gist, a perception's lines of what you came to know by it), with the size of the whole. whole, or left out: each entry whole."
  who: "Leave it out: this reads your own record. Asked of anyone else, it answers why not."
  question: "A question about what this call reads. A reader reads the answer whole (each entry whole, unless you name a how) and answers it: you are given its answer and none of the record."
---
Reads your own record as it stands now, and nobody else's. Your outline lists what you were not handed whole, each line with its size, and this opens it. Each entry comes with its id and, where the story keeps time, its date. A size is in tokens, so you know what a call brings before you make it. What you perceived comes as it reached you, and only while you have not taken it in: once you have, what you kept of it is in your memories. A memory that has faded comes by its gist, marked faint; recall is what brings one back in full. What you know comes as statements; a secret you hold is said in the lore you are given as your own. An answer that does not hold everything it matched says how much it shows of how much, and the call that reads on.

Asked with a question, it hands its answer to a reader and gives you what the reader says in its place.
